idiom_name: rule table (condition + action records) + facts/working memory + bounded match-and-fire loop
implementation_notes: Language-neutral form: represent each rule as data - a condition over facts plus an action - keep the rules in one collection that the host loads and replaces as a unit, and run a bounded evaluate-act loop: match conditions against the current facts, order the matched rules by a declared precedence, fire one action, then re-evaluate the facts it changed. Facts are the shared working memory; only actions mutate them, and each mutation either re-triggers evaluation (forward chaining) or is marked non-repeatable (refraction / no-loop). Add indexing or a discrimination network only when the rule count makes a naive scan too slow; below a few dozen rules the scan is clearer and fast enough.
code_sketch:
rules = load_rule_base(source)      # data: (name, condition(facts), action(facts), salience)
facts = assemble_facts(request)     # working memory
for _ in range(max_cycles):
    matched = [r for r in rules if r.condition(facts) and not r.fired]
    if not matched:
        break
    rule = pick(matched)            # declared precedence: salience, recency, order
    rule.action(facts)              # only actions mutate facts
    rule.fired = True               # refraction: no re-fire on unchanged facts
pitfalls: Letting the rule base become a general-purpose program (loops, sequencing, orchestration): the result is an untyped, unrefactorable second codebase.
No termination policy: a rule that re-asserts the facts it matched loops until an iteration cap - bound the cycles and make rules non-repeatable.
Implicit precedence: without a declared conflict-resolution rule, which rule fires first depends on load order or engine internals.

Wrong move: authoring rule expressions against fact fields the rule writer guessed at -> a renamed or misspelled field never matches, so the rule silently stops deciding instead of failing -> validate every rule against the fact schema on load (typed inputs/known fields, strict type checking as Rego or typed engine settings give) and fail fast on unknown fields and operators.
